svg.title: Little’s law connects matched averages, not peak capacity
svg.desc: Constructed four-job cohort • 20 ms horizon • all four followed through exit at 20
svg.text: Little’s law connects matched averages, not peak capacity
Constructed four-job cohort • 20 ms horizon • all four followed through exit at 20
System occupancy: area over time
Area 44 request-ms; mean L = 44/20 = 2.2
Residence times 5,9,13,17 ms; mean 11
200 requests/s × 0.011 s = 2.2 requests
Queue-only: stop at service start
Waits 0,4,8,12 ms; total area 24
Mean Lq = 1.2; mean wait = 6 ms
200 requests/s × 0.006 s = 1.2 requests
One visit and one serial worker here
Service 5 ms per job; worker busy 20 ms
System mean = queue mean + 1 active job
Request population is not GPU utilization
Means cannot guarantee a safe maximum
Mean requests 2.2; peak requests 4
Rounding mean up gives 3, below the peak
No p99 or physical-byte bound follows
Terminal at 20 is included in cohort follow-up, not in a [0,20) departure counter.
The exact finite-cohort identity is not evidence of sustainable serving capacity.
